title: Residue reduction is conservative on locally complete objects
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative Noetherian ring, J an ideal and U an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Use completed coefficients and reductions of [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. Let T,M in D(B_X|U) both be locally complete for ker(q_0). If f:T -> M has invertible derived residue reduction R_0(f), then f is invertible. No constructibility, boundedness, finite Tor amplitude, or perfectness of the quotients over A is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09C6, final complete-cone argument; Algebraization Tags 099M and 099F for quotient completion and derived Nakayama.

proof.text: Choose the universally specified derived change-of-rings cochain model for the residue projection. Its exactness and uniqueness of left derived functors transport a triangulated shift structure to the actual adicResidueLocalReduction. Complete f to a distinguished triangle T -> M -> Q. On each further slice each defining internal-Hom completeness test is an exact functor. Its first two values vanish, so its cone value vanishes. Thus Q is locally complete. Exact residue reduction and the zero-cone criterion give R_0(Q)=0.

Induct on n. The base R_0(Q)=0 was just obtained. Apply the successor coefficient-vanishing theorem to R_0(Q)=0 and R_n(Q)=0 to obtain R_(n+1)(Q)=0. This is the consecutive coefficient triangle part of the original plan, with no completeness or finiteness conditions on Q.

Apply the normalized complete-reduction cone theorem to Q. Every term F_n is isomorphic to exact scalar restriction of the zero object R_n(Q), hence is zero. The homotopy-limit Hom vanishing criterion makes the identity of the cone point zero: all maps from it and its shift to each zero F_n vanish. Therefore the cone point and Q are zero. The original distinguished triangle makes f invertible.
